The diagram shows the eight vertices of an octagon connected by line segments. Jodhvir wants to write one of the integers 1,2,3 or 4 at each of the vertices so that the two integers at the ends of every line segment are different. He has already written three integers as shown.
<image1>
How many times will the integer 4 appear in his completed diagram?

Observing these line segments, the connection relationship is complete connection between two alternating groups of vertices: one group is {A, C, E, G}, the other group is {B, D, F, H}, and there are no line segments connecting vertices within the same group. Reasoning: The problem requires that the integers at the two ends of each line segment be different, and the integers can only be chosen from 1, 2, 3, 4. In the figure A, C, E are already 1, 2, 3 respectively. Since each of B, D, F, H is connected to A, C, E, they cannot be filled with 1, 2, 3, and can only be filled with 4. Therefore the four vertices B, D, F, H must all be 4. The remaining G is connected to B, D, F, H, and these points are all 4, so G cannot be 4. Thus the integer 4 appears a total of 4 times.

method.method_draft: First describe the image by labeling the octagon vertices clockwise: A is the top vertex marked 1, B upper-right, C right marked 2, D lower-right, E bottom marked 3, F lower-left, G left, H upper-left. From the line segments in the diagram, recognize the graph as the complete bipartite graph with alternating parts {A,C,E,G} and {B,D,F,H}: each vertex in one part is connected to every vertex in the other part, and there are no segments within a part. From the text, use that adjacent vertices must receive different numbers from {1,2,3,4}. Since A,C,E already have colors 1,2,3 and every vertex B,D,F,H is adjacent to all three of A,C,E, each of B,D,F,H must be 4. The remaining vertex G is in the same part as A,C,E and is adjacent to the four forced 4s, so it cannot be 4. Therefore 4 appears exactly four times.
